userStories.title: Expose the Agent id in project roster responses
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry the actual Agent row id through the project roster repository, DTO, committed OpenAPI and regenerated CLI types.

**Motivation** — R2-22: the timeline actor falls back to the raw id for agents: `useProjectMemberNames.nameOf` resolves users only, and `GET /projects/:slug/agents` (`ProjectAgentDto`) carries no agent `id` to map from.

**Approach** — API `apps/api/src/agents/prisma-agent.repository.ts` `findProjectRoster(projectId)` already selects `agent.id` (it maps memberships by `principalId`); it just does not return it.

- API `apps/api/src/agents/dto/project-agent.dto.ts`
  - Baseline: `ProjectAgentRecord` and `ProjectAgentDto` have no `id`.
  - Target: both gain `id: string` (the Agent row id); `ProjectAgentDto.from` copies it and the DTO declares it with `@ApiProperty()`. `findProjectRoster` returns `id: row.agent.id`. `openapi.json` and the CLI types are regenerated with `bun run generate` from the repo root, never hand-edited.

The existing `src/agents/prisma-agent.repository.find-roster.spec.ts` keys agent ids by slug, so the id test goes in a new spec (see Creates); the controller route spec is `src/projects/projects.controller.spec.ts`.

**Scope** — In: record/DTO field, repository return mapping, regenerated root OpenAPI and CLI types, and the three new unit specs. Out: US-002 owns web lookup and display. The project agent roster DTO gains only `id`; no other API field, route or permission changes. No migration is needed.

**Interface** — `ProjectAgentRecord` and `ProjectAgentDto` gain `id: string`; DTO uses `@ApiProperty()`; repository returns `id: row.agent.id`.

**Test implementation notes** — Create src/agents/dto/project-agent.dto.spec.ts, src/agents/project-agent-openapi.contract.spec.ts and src/agents/prisma-agent.repository.roster-id.spec.ts. Use mocked Prisma/transaction collaborators, Agent id agent-1 and slug bot. Mirror src/fleet/fleet-openapi.contract.spec.ts for committed schema parsing. Preserve existing roster/controller assertions; also exercise the existing empty-membership return of [] in the roster-id harness for the negative-path regression criterion. Adjust typed fixtures if the new required id demands it. Run bun run generate from the repository root despite the binding apps/api workdir; openapi.json and apps/cli/src/generated/types.gen.ts are modified generated artifacts, not new files to hand-author.
acceptanceCriteria: ProjectAgentDto.from returns a DTO whose id is 'agent-1' when given a record with id 'agent-1', slug 'bot' and the other roster fields.

findProjectRoster('proj-1') returns a record whose id is 'agent-1' and slug is 'bot' when the Prisma client returns one AGENT membership whose principalId is 'agent-1' and one agent row whose id is 'agent-1' and slug is 'bot'.
When committed openapi.json is parsed using the pattern of src/fleet/fleet-openapi.contract.spec.ts, the ProjectAgentDto schema has an id property of type string and lists id in its required array.
findProjectRoster('proj-1') returns an empty array when the project has no AGENT memberships, preserving the existing empty-roster behavior.

routing.reasoning: Additive field through an existing repository/DTO and standard generation flow; no authorization, routing or database behavior changes.

modifiedFiles.reason: regenerated by `bun run generate` from the repo root so `ProjectAgentDto` lists `id`; never hand-edited.
the CLI types regenerated by bun run generate together with the root OpenAPI document, so ProjectAgentDto gains id; never hand-edited.

userStories.title: Name agents on timeline and memory pages
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve rostered agent ids to names in timeline actors and memory subject labels, including the retire dialog.

**Motivation** — R2-23: the memory Retire dialog body reads "You are retiring: agent:<id>" (the raw subject) while the row shows "Agent cmutp0nw" (a short id, not the agent's name).

**Approach** — `lib/memory-subject.ts` `memorySubject(subject)` returns `{ type: 'ticket' | 'agent' | 'other', id, short }`. `composables/useProjectMemberNames.ts` `useProjectMemberNames(slug)` returns `{ members, load, nameOf }`; `nameOf(userId)` returns the member's name or email, the signed-in user's, or null.

- `composables/useProjectAgents.ts` `ProjectAgent` gains `id: string`.
- `composables/useProjectAgentNames.ts` (new) `useProjectAgentNames(slug)` returns `{ agents, load, nameOf }`.
  `load()` reads `GET /projects/:slug/agents` through `useApi()` and stores the response `items` in `agents`; `nameOf(agentId)` returns the roster agent's `name` for that `id`, else null. A failed `load()` rejects; callers catch it and keep falling back (see Failure Handling).
- `pages/[project]/timeline.vue` `actorName(actorId)`
  - Baseline: `memberNames.nameOf(actorId) ?? actorId`.
  - Target: `memberNames.nameOf(actorId) ?? agentNames.nameOf(actorId) ?? actorId`; the page calls `agentNames.load()` on mount beside `memberNames.load()`, each with its own `.catch`.
- `pages/[project]/memory.vue` subject label
  - Baseline: an agent subject renders `t('memory.subject.agent') + ' ' + subject.short`; the retire dialog gets `:item-label="retireTarget?.subject"` (raw).
  - Target: one page function `subjectLabel(item)` gives `Agent <name>` when `agentNames.nameOf(id)` resolves, else `Agent <short>`; `Ticket <short>` for a ticket subject; the raw subject otherwise. The row text and the dialog `item-label` both use it. The row keeps its `:title="item.subject"`, the ticket link, and the `{{ item.subject }}` mustache of the `v-else` branch for an other-type subject. The page calls `useProjectAgentNames(slug)` as an auto-imported composable (no explicit import), as `timeline.vue` calls `useProjectMemberNames`.

**Failure Handling** — `agentNames.load()` rejects (no permission, network): No toast. Timeline shows the raw actor id; memory shows `Agent <short>` in the row and the dialog.

**Scope** — In: web roster id shape, the new lookup composable, timeline/memory consumers and harness adaptations. Out: API field propagation/generation belongs to US-001; other page polish belongs to US-003 through US-007. Agent names come only from the project agent roster; an agent no longer on the roster shows its raw id (timeline) or short id (memory). Memory retirement permissions and sequencing remain unchanged.

**Interface** — `ProjectAgent` gains `id: string`; `useProjectAgentNames(slug)` returns `{ agents, load, nameOf }`; `subjectLabel(item)` is the single page label function.

**Test implementation notes** — Add use-project-agent-names.spec.ts, timeline-agent-actor.spec.ts and memory-agent-subject.spec.ts. The new page tests mount with real names-composable wiring and a stubbed agents API, not a nameOf stub. Stub memory.decision.retire as in memory-retire-visibility.spec.ts. Add `{ nameOf: () => null, load: async () => undefined }` as useProjectAgentNames in memory-readable.spec.ts, memory-retire-visibility.spec.ts, memory-retire-flow.spec.ts, memory-mount.spec.ts, timeline-readable.spec.ts and filter-select-height.spec.ts using each harness's existing globals/aliases, so no extra request occurs and every assertion stays. In tests/pages/memory.spec.ts add `subjectLabel: (item) => item.subject` to createRenderContext and retain the source assertion for the other-type mustache.
acceptanceCriteria: When useProjectAgentNames('web').load() is called, it calls GET /projects/web/agents through useApi().
After load() resolves with items [{ id: 'agent-1', name: 'Probe Bot', slug: 'probe' }], nameOf('agent-1') returns 'Probe Bot'.
After the same load, nameOf('agent-2') returns null.

When pages/[project]/timeline.vue mounts with one event whose actorId is 'agent-1', the members API returning no matching member and the agents API returning { items: [{ id: 'agent-1', name: 'Probe Bot' }] }, that event's actor cell renders 'Probe Bot'.
On the same timeline mount, an event whose actorId is 'user-1' and whose member name is 'Ada' still renders 'Ada' in its actor cell.
When the timeline page mounts with the agents API rejecting, it renders raw 'agent-1' in the actor cell and shows no error toast for the agents read.

When pages/[project]/memory.vue mounts with permission memory.decision.retire as in tests/pages/memory-retire-visibility.spec.ts, an active DECISION item whose subject is 'agent:agent-1' and the agents API returning { items: [{ id: 'agent-1', name: 'Probe Bot' }] }, that row's subject cell renders 'Agent Probe Bot'.
On that memory mount, opening the item's Retire dialog passes 'Agent Probe Bot' as the dialog's item-label.
When the memory page mounts with the agents API rejecting, the row renders 'Agent agent-1' (the first 8 characters of the id) and its Retire dialog receives the same text as item-label.
Given the same permission stub, opening the Retire dialog for an active DECISION item whose subject is 'ticket:ticket-123456789' passes 'Ticket ticket-1' as item-label.
When agentNames.load() rejects on the memory page because of permission or network failure, no toast is shown for that read.

userStories.title: Clarify settings headings and isolate project deletion
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Correct project settings headings and put deletion in a separate bottom Danger zone card.

**Motivation** — R2-9: `components/SettingsProjectCard.vue` puts the destructive "Delete Project" button beside "Save Project" in the same form row.

**Approach** — R2-9 = Delete Project moves to a separate "Danger zone" card at the bottom of the Project tab and keeps its confirm.

- `pages/[project]/settings.vue`
  - Baseline: `PageHeader :title="t('vcs.title')"`; first tab `t('projects.title')`; the first card heading `t('projects.settings.title')`; no danger zone.
  - Target: `PageHeader :title="t('projects.settings.title')"` ("Project Settings"); first tab `t('projects.settings.tab')` (new, "General" / "常规"); the first card heading `t('projects.settings.detailsTitle')` (new, "Project details" / "项目详情"). The VCS tab keeps its own `vcs.title` heading. Last in the Project tab, after the memory card and only once `projectData` loaded, renders `SettingsDangerZoneCard` with `:project="projectData"`.
- `components/SettingsDangerZoneCard.vue` (new) — a `rounded-md border border-destructive/50 p-6 space-y-4` card, `data-testid="settings-danger-zone"`, heading `t('projects.settings.dangerZone.title')` ("Danger zone"), text `t('projects.settings.dangerZone.description')` ("Deleting a project removes its tickets, settings and history. This cannot be undone."), and the destructive `projects.settings.delete` button, `data-testid="project-delete"`. Its `deleteProject()` is the one moved out of `SettingsProjectCard` unchanged: `window.confirm(t('projects.settings.deleteConfirm'))`, then $api.delete(apiPath`/projects/${props.project.slug}`), success toast, `useRouter().push('/')`; on error `toast.error(extractApiError(err))`.
- `components/SettingsProjectCard.vue` keeps only the Save button in its button row; `deleteProject` and `deletingProject` move to the new card.

Every new user-facing string gets a key in both `i18n/locales/en.json` and `i18n/locales/zh.json`.

**Failure Handling** — Delete project fails: Error toast (`extractApiError`); the page stays.

**Scope** — In: settings title/tab/card headings, new danger card, moved delete behavior and locale keys. Out: settings form-select polish belongs to US-007; agent naming belongs to US-002. Delete Project keeps the `window.confirm` dialog; no typed-name confirmation is added. Save fields, save behavior and VCS heading remain unchanged.

**Interface** — `SettingsDangerZoneCard` consumes `:project="projectData"`; `deleteProject()` and `deletingProject` move to it unchanged. The API call is $api.delete(apiPath`/projects/${props.project.slug}`).

**Test implementation notes** — Add settings-danger-zone-card.spec.ts and settings-page-title.spec.ts. For the page ordering assertion register the real SettingsDangerZoneCard rather than a uiStubs placeholder, proving it renders last after memory once projectData loads. Keep existing settings-project-card.spec.ts name/description/brief save assertions and the VCS e2e heading check. Modify tests/openapi/web-gap-ops.spec.ts to inspect the new danger card for DELETE while retaining page GET and project-card PATCH checks.
acceptanceCriteria: When pages/[project]/settings.vue mounts, PageHeader renders with title 'Project Settings'.
On that mount, the first tab trigger with value 'project' reads 'General'.
On that mount, the first card heading reads 'Project details'.
Once the project loads, the Project tab renders settings-danger-zone after the memory card as the last child of the Project tab content.
When SettingsProjectCard mounts with a project, it renders no 'Delete Project' button.
When SettingsDangerZoneCard mounts with project slug 'web', it renders the 'Danger zone' heading and a project-delete button reading 'Delete Project'.
When project-delete is clicked with window.confirm returning true, $api.delete is called with '/projects/web', the projects.settings.deleted success toast is shown and the router is pushed to '/'.
When project-delete is clicked with window.confirm returning false, no $api.delete call is made.
When project-delete is clicked and $api.delete rejects, extractApiError of that error is shown as an error toast and the router is not pushed.

routing.reasoning: Standard component extraction and heading changes move an existing mutation flow unchanged; no authorization or API semantics change.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test "project settings uses GET/PATCH/DELETE /projects/:slug" asserts the project DELETE call lives in the SettingsProjectCard component; the delete now lives in the new SettingsDangerZoneCard component, so the test reads that component's source for the DELETE call and keeps the GET (page) and PATCH (project card) checks.

userStories.title: Compact ticket assignment and improve detail readability
userStories.description: **Goal** — Collapse assignment controls, remove the description gap, label fleet commands and format comment timestamps. **Motivation** — R2-11: `components/TicketProperties.vue` always renders `AssigneePicker`, a search box plus 9+ option rows, in the properties rail. The ticket page grid in `pages/[project]/tickets/[ref].vue` has the rail span two rows, so a tall rail stretches row 1 and leaves an empty gap between Fleet runs and the description. `components/TicketFleetRuns.vue` shows the command as the raw code (`RUN`). **Approach** — R2-11 = collapsed assignee picker (current assignee + Change, list on demand, closes after a pick). - `components/TicketProperties.vue` assignee block (when `canAssign`) - Baseline: `AssigneePicker` and the Unassign button always render under the assignee row. - Target: a `pickerOpen` ref (false). Closed: an outline `size="sm"` button `data-testid="assignee-change"` (`t('tickets.assignee.change')`, new, "Change" / "更改") beside the Unassign button; no `AssigneePicker`. Clicking Change sets `pickerOpen` true: `AssigneePicker` renders with a ghost `size="sm"` button `data-testid="assignee-cancel"` (`t('common.cancel')`) that sets it false. A successful `onAssigneeSelect` sets `pickerOpen` false; a failed one leaves it open. - `pages/[project]/tickets/[ref].vue` grid - Baseline: `grid grid-cols-1 gap-6 lg:grid-cols-3 lg:items-start`. - Target: adds `lg:grid-rows-[auto_1fr]`, so the rail's extra height goes to row 2 and row 1 stays as tall as the header and fleet runs. - `components/TicketFleetRuns.vue` command chip: `codeLabel(t, te, 'fleet.command', row.run.command)`, with `const { t, te } = useI18n()`. - `lib/format-date-time.ts` (new) `formatDateTime(iso: string, locale: string | undefined)` returns `new Date(iso).toLocaleString(locale, { year: 'numeric', month: 'short', day: 'numeric', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' })`, or `iso` unchanged when it does not parse to a valid date. - `components/CommentThread.vue` comment time - Baseline: `{{ comment.createdAt }}`. - Target: `{{ formatDateTime(comment.createdAt, commentLocale()) }}`, with `const { t, locale } = useI18n()` and a script helper `commentLocale = () => unref(locale)` (templates unwrap the destructured ref, so the template must not read `.value`). An i18n stub without `locale` (the existing CommentThread specs use `enI18n()`, which returns only `t` and `te`) gives `undefined`, which formats in the runtime default locale. `lib/fleet-i18n.ts` `codeLabel(t, te, prefix, code)` returns `t(prefix + '.' + code)` when that key exists, else `code`. `fleet.command.*` keys exist for `AGENT RUN PLAN CONFIG_EDIT CONFIG_DRIFT REVIEW FIX THREAD` (`RUN` = "Run"). Every new user-facing string gets a key in both `i18n/locales/en.json` and `i18n/locales/zh.json`. **Failure Handling** — `formatDateTime` gets a value that is not a valid date: Returns the value unchanged. Assign request fails: Error toast as today (`extractApiError`); the picker stays open. **Scope** — In: assignment disclosure state, ticket grid class, fleet command chip and time utility/component integration. Out: US-005 owns job detail/progress; US-003 owns settings; US-007 owns raw select styling. The Unassign button keeps its current visibility rule. Measured sizes, alignment and wrapping are checked in the post-merge live sweep on koda-wk, not in unit tests (jsdom has no layout). **Interface** — `formatDateTime(iso: string, locale: string | undefined)`; `commentLocale = () => unref(locale)`; `codeLabel(t, te, 'fleet.command', row.run.command)`; `pickerOpen` starts false and changes on Change, Cancel and successful selection. **Test implementation notes** — Add format-date-time.spec.ts, ticket-assignee-collapsed.spec.ts, comment-thread-time.spec.ts and ticket-detail-grid.spec.ts. Use the real date utility in component mounts and compare en/zh output in the runtime timezone. Update ticket-fleet-runs.spec.ts expectation RUN to Run; update project-permission-gates.spec.ts ticket.assign case and negative control to expect assignee-change rather than assignee-search while retaining Unassign, label, link and delete checks; update ticket-detail-operations.e2e.spec.ts to click Change before search. Preserve the assigning concurrency guard and existing permission flags. Existing CommentThread stubs without locale and fixtures with createdAt now remain supported.
acceptanceCriteria: When TicketProperties mounts with canAssign true, it renders assignee-change reading 'Change' and no assignee-search input.
When assignee-change is clicked, AssigneePicker renders with assignee-search present and an assignee-cancel button.
Given the picker is open, clicking assignee-cancel removes assignee-search.
Given the picker is open, picking an option whose assign POST resolves removes assignee-search because the picker closes.
Given the picker is open, picking an option whose assign POST rejects keeps assignee-search rendered and shows the extractApiError error toast.
When TicketProperties mounts with canAssign false, it renders neither assignee-change nor assignee-search.
When pages/[project]/tickets/[ref].vue mounts with a loaded ticket, its page grid has class lg:grid-rows-[auto_1fr].
When TicketFleetRuns mounts with a run whose command is 'RUN', that row's ticket-fleet-run-command chip renders 'Run'.

When CommentThread mounts with an i18n locale ref holding 'en' and a comment whose createdAt is '2026-11-10T14:07:45.657Z', comment-time is a time element whose datetime is '2026-11-10T14:07:45.657Z' and whose text equals formatDateTime('2026-11-10T14:07:45.657Z', 'en'); with the locale ref holding 'zh' instead, the text equals formatDateTime('2026-11-10T14:07:45.657Z', 'zh').
formatDateTime('2026-11-10T14:07:45.657Z', 'en') returns a string including 'Nov' and '2026' and not including 'T14'.
formatDateTime('now', 'en') returns 'now'.

routing.reasoning: Small disclosure-state, label, date-helper and grid changes use established patterns; strict isolation is retained for the permission-gated assignment entry point and its explicit canAssign negative-path assertions.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test asserting the `ticket-fleet-run-command` chip text is `RUN` now expects the label `Run`, the `fleet.command.RUN` translation.

the US-007 AC-1 test expects `assignee-search` with only `ticket.assign`; the picker is now collapsed, so the test expects the `assignee-change` button instead (and its control case expects no `assignee-change`), keeping the Unassign, label, link and delete checks.
the assign step fills `assignee-search` directly; it now clicks `assignee-change` first, then fills `assignee-search` and picks the option as before.

userStories.title: Align job grids and hide inactive or empty fields
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Use consistent three-column job grids and show only applicable live and populated metadata.

**Motivation** — R1-16: job detail stacks a 4-column grid (`FleetJobProgress`) over a 3-column one, and a finished job shows Progress, Current story, Phase and Last heartbeat as `-` plus several other empty `-` fields.

**Approach** — R1-16 = one consistent 3-column grid, live-only fields (Progress, Current story, Phase, Last heartbeat) only while the job is active, other empty fields hidden.

`lib/fleet-jobs.ts` `isActiveJobState(state)` is true for `QUEUED ASSIGNED RUNNING UPLOADING`.

- `components/fleet/FleetJobProgress.vue`
  - Baseline: `grid grid-cols-2 ... sm:grid-cols-4`; Progress, Current story, Phase and Cost always render.
  - Target: `grid grid-cols-1 gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm sm:grid-cols-3`; the Progress, Current story and Phase items render only when `isActiveJobState(job.state)`; Cost always renders.
- `pages/[project]/fleet/jobs/[id]/index.vue` detail `dl` (already `sm:grid-cols-3`)
  - Baseline: every item renders, empty values as `-`.
  - Target: Runner, Requester, Bash (non-config job) and Queued always render. Last heartbeat renders only when the job is active. Profiles only when `job.profiles` is non-empty; Started only when `startedAt`; Finished only when `finishedAt`; Finish result only when `finishResult` (and not a config job); Branch only when `resultBranch` or the WIP-push status (`wipPush`) is set, since that `dd` is the only place the push status shows; Pull request only when `prUrl` or `resultPrUrl`. Plan from and Tickets keep their conditions.

Preserve the existing non-config Profiles exclusion while adding its non-empty check. Gate whole field items, including labels. Keep safePrUrl linking and the plain-text resultPrUrl fallback.

**Scope** — In: FleetJobProgress grid/active fields and job detail dl visibility. Out: ticket details belong to US-004; flow and notification wording belongs to US-006. Job detail: the Plan from and Tickets items, the pipeline and the open-items panel keep their current conditions. Measured sizes, alignment and wrapping are checked in the post-merge live sweep on koda-wk, not in unit tests (jsdom has no layout). No state transitions or action authorization changes.

**Interface** — Reuse `isActiveJobState(state)` and existing `job`, `prUrl` and `wipPush`; do not duplicate active-state definitions.

**Test implementation notes** — Add tests/pages/fleet-job-detail-fields.spec.ts using the fleet-job-detail.spec.ts mount harness and fixtures for active/completed/cancelled-with-WIP. Add `state: 'RUNNING'` to tests/components/fleet-job-progress.spec.ts job() fixture, retaining all existing assertions; extend mounts for terminal rendering and grid classes. Existing fleet-job-stories.spec.ts is a different surface and needs no change. Existing fleet-dispatch e2e cost, RUNNING story and populated completed finish/PR checks remain applicable.
acceptanceCriteria: When FleetJobProgress mounts with a RUNNING job, it renders fleet-job-progress, fleet-job-story, fleet-job-phase and fleet-job-cost.
When FleetJobProgress mounts with a COMPLETED job, it renders fleet-job-cost and none of fleet-job-progress, fleet-job-story or fleet-job-phase.
FleetJobProgress renders its dl with classes grid-cols-1 and sm:grid-cols-3 and without sm:grid-cols-4.
When the job detail page mounts with a COMPLETED job whose lastHeartbeatAt is set, it renders no Last heartbeat item: the fleet.jobs.detail.heartbeat label is absent.
When the job detail page mounts with a RUNNING job whose lastHeartbeatAt is set, it renders the Last heartbeat item.

When the job detail page mounts with a COMPLETED job whose profiles is empty and whose finishResult, resultBranch, resultPrUrl and startedAt are null, it renders none of the Profiles, Finish result, Branch, Pull request or Started labels.
On that mount, the Runner, Requester and Queued labels still render.
When the job detail page mounts with a COMPLETED job whose finishResult is 'promoted' and resultBranch is 'feat/x', it renders Finish result reading 'promoted' and Branch reading 'feat/x'.
When the job detail page mounts with a CANCELLED RUN job whose resultBranch is null and wipPush is 'failed:auth', it renders the Branch item with the fleet.jobs.detail.wipPush.failed text.

routing.reasoning: Two existing display surfaces use standard field conditions and the existing active-state helper; no new abstraction, authorization or workflow change.

modifiedFiles.reason: the `job()` fixture has no `state`, so Progress, Current story and Phase would no longer render; the fixture gains `state: 'RUNNING'` and every existing assertion stays.

userStories.title: Explain flow stop reasons and KB empty states
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Show localized flow titles and stop reasons across inbox, bell and flow detail, and instructional KB empty states.

**Motivation** — R2-14: `flow_stopped` and `flow_questions` have no `notifications.kinds.*` key, so the inbox row and the bell show the API's English fallback title and, for `flow_stopped`, its server body (`SPEC_REVIEW job cmw82wqnx...: no verdict JSON in the agent output`): a raw step code and a raw job id. The flow detail page shows `flow.stopReason` raw (`verdict_unreadable`).

**Approach** — `lib/notifications.ts` `notificationText(n, i18n)` words a notification from `notifications.kinds.<kind>` with `n.params`, else returns `n.title`. `lib/humanize-code.ts` `humanizeCode(code)` turns `verdict_unreadable` into `Verdict unreadable`. `lib/fleet-i18n.ts` `codeLabel(t, te, prefix, code)` returns `t(prefix + '.' + code)` when that key exists, else `code`.

API flow stop reasons (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-step-decision.ts` `FlowStopReason` plus the service's `human_stop` and `approval_rejected`): `step_failed verdict_unreadable review_findings review_ambiguous calls_failed plan_no_result run_no_pr pr_not_ready cost_cap creator_lost_access budget_paused dispatch_refused pr_closed spec_changed human_stop approval_rejected`. The `flow_stopped` notification params are `{ flowId, feature, stopReason }`; `flow_questions` params are `{ flowId, feature, step, count }`.

- `lib/notifications.ts` gains `notificationDetail(n, i18n)`: for kind `flow_stopped` with a string `params.stopReason`, `codeLabel(t, te, 'fleet.flows.stopReason', stopReason)` but with `humanizeCode(stopReason)` in place of the raw code when no key exists; for every other kind, `n.body`.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add user status chips and aligned actions, keep audit project labels on one line and standardize the 16 remaining scoped selects at 40px.

**Motivation** — R2-18: admin users shows Role as a chip but Status as plain text, and the "Edit roles" button (with an icon) sits 2 px higher than "Disable" in the same cell (live: top 362 vs 364 px at 1440 px).

- `pages/admin/users.vue`
  - Status cell, baseline: plain text. Target: `<Badge variant="outline" data-testid="user-status-chip" :data-status="user.disabled ? 'disabled' : 'active'">` with a leading dot `span` (`h-1.5 w-1.5 rounded-full`, `bg-status-done` when active, `bg-status-rejected` when disabled, `aria-hidden="true"`) and the same `admin.users.status.*` text.
  - Actions cell, baseline: `<TableCell class="space-x-2 text-right">` with the buttons inline. Target: the cell holds one `div` `data-testid="user-actions"` with class `flex items-center justify-end gap-2`, and the Disable/Enable button gains `data-testid="user-toggle-disabled"`.
- `pages/admin/audit.vue` Project `TableCell` (the one holding the existing `audit-project` button, which keeps its testid): adds `whitespace-nowrap` and `data-testid="audit-project-cell"`.
- The 16 raw selects use `FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS` in place of their `h-9`/`h-8 rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-2|px-3 text-sm` base, keeping their other classes and every id, `data-testid`, binding and handler:

| file | select(s) | extra classes kept |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `components/fleet/threads/BackendPicker.vue` | `#thread-backend-agent`, `#thread-backend-model`, `#thread-backend-effort` | `w-full` |

| `components/PrincipalRolesDialog.vue` | `binding-role-select` | `w-full` |

**Scope** — In: the two admin templates and exactly these 16 selects in seven files.
